title: Paella
description:
“Pie Eh Ugh! – Pie Eh Ugh! – Pie Eh Ugh!” And so Lauren and Andrea chanted, as they marched around the kitchen with their signs attached to yardsticks (maybe also with placards saying “Down With Paella, Up With Mac ‘n Cheese.”)
I guess they just didn’t appreciate what a wonderful treat this is, probably the most famous dish of Spain, and certainly one of our favorites. They did not prevail that night, eating their dinner (as always) and over the years they have greatly expanded their culinary horizons (even trying – and loving – “foie gras soup” at a fancy little Parisian restaurant late one night on our first trip to France with them.)
Maybe one day they will even make this Paella recipe for themselves and their kids!
There are as many Paella recipes as there are cooks, but the constants are rice, olive oil, and saffron (maybe chorizo), plus whatever you love from the land or sea, served in a big dish. We got our Paella dish as a special first Christmas present from Grandma and Grandpa Jackson, who introduced us to Paella. We still use the recipe from the box – of course with our own variations!
Paella
Although the list of ingredients is long, most of the work can be done ahead of time. Since this Paella is a complete meal it needs little accompaniment, maybe a simple salad and crusty bread.
ingredients: First prepare the lobster, shrimp, and chicken.
directions: Without removing the lobster shell, cut the tail crosswise into 1-2 inch slices, from underneath.
Season the chicken with the salt, pepper, thyme, and paprika.
Then brown it in a skillet with a ¼ cup oil, about 2-3 minutes on each side.
Remove the chicken to a plate when done.
Cook the lobster in the skillet over high heat for 2-3 minutes, until the shell begins to turn pink. Set it aside.
Pour boiling chicken broth (to which the saffron has been added) over the rice, stirring constantly.
Add the sofrito and continue to stir until well blended. Adjust the seasonings to taste.
Transfer the rice mixture to the paella dish. Arrange the chicken, lobster, shrimp, and chorizo. Then scatter the peas on top.
Set the dish on the lower shelf of the oven and bake uncovered for 25-30 minutes, until all the liquid has been absorbed.
Do not stir the rice once it goes into the oven.
About 45 minutes before you plan to serve the Paella, preheat the oven to 400 degrees.
In a big frying pan, sauté the rice in 4 tablespoons of olive oil until translucent.
When the Paella is done (the rice should still be a little al dente), remove the dish from the oven and cover loosely with a kitchen towel.
Let it rest for 5 minutes or so, to let the flavors get fully absorbed.
Garnish with some lemon wedges and serve the Paella at the table directly from the dish.
No “Ughs!” only “Yums!”
To make the sofrito, first discard all the fat from the skillet, then add ¼ cup of olive oil and heat it.
Quickly brown the pork on all sides, 1-2 minutes,
Add the onions, garlic, pepper strips, and tomato. Cook until most of liquid evaporates, stirring constantly.
When the mixture is thick, set the sofrito aside.
